cross_layer.title: VLAN 30: single-fiber uplink to a sole gateway
cross_layer.detail: VLAN 30's only L3 gateway is core1 (no FHRP); access1 Gi0/1 reach the fabric over a single non-redundant fiber.
cross_layer.recommendation: A single fiber cut isolates the VLAN with no L1 path and no L3 backup - add a redundant uplink AND an FHRP peer.

cross_layer.title: core1: stacked single point of failure across L1, L3
cross_layer.detail: core1 is implicated at multiple layers at once (L1, L3) - its loss compounds physical, switching, and/or routing failure.
cross_layer.recommendation: Treat as a top migration risk: stage redundancy at every implicated layer before cutover.

cross_layer.title: VLAN 30: sole gateway core1 with no FHRP
cross_layer.detail: core1 is the only in-scan L3 gateway for VLAN 30; loss drops the default gateway for every VLAN 30 host.
cross_layer.recommendation: Add an FHRP peer (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) or confirm a redundant off-scan gateway.

cross_layer.title: core1: L1 fault on an L3 gateway switch

cross_layer.recommendation: Investigate the affected port; instability here affects every VLAN gatewayed by this switch.

framework_coverage.note: Config-evidenced mapping of the engine's hardening checks to framework controls — NOT a full framework audit. Controls outside this check set are not auto-assessed (never assumed 'pass'); a not-applicable check stays 'na'.

detectors.title: Err-disabled physical port
detectors.checks: A physical port whose status matches an err-disable state (a protection mechanism shut the port down).
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or interface status/counters not captured for the port

detectors.title: Half-duplex trunk / uplink
detectors.checks: A trunk or uplink port negotiated to half-duplex (a duplex mismatch on an inter-switch link).
detectors.threshold: duplex == Half (on a trunk or uplink port)
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or the interface detail carrying duplex not captured

detectors.title: Single-fiber (non-redundant) uplink
detectors.checks: An uplink with only one physical fiber member — no link-level redundancy, so the next fiber cut isolates the switch.
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or the topology/interface evidence for the uplink absent

detectors.title: High interface error/drop rate
detectors.checks: An operationally-up port carrying non-zero input errors, CRCs, output drops, output errors or late collisions (a marginal cable/optic).
detectors.healthy_value: zero error/drop counters on up ports
detectors.threshold: any counter > 0 (input_errors / crc_errors / output_drops / output_errors / late_collisions)
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or interface counters not captured (counters absent != zero)

detectors.title: Single-gateway VLAN (no redundant first hop)
detectors.checks: A VLAN whose default gateway SVI exists on only one scanned switch — one box owns the first hop, a single point of failure.
detectors.abstains_when: no device carrying the VLAN's SVI was collected (an off-scan gateway is not evidence of absence)

detectors.title: Multi-gateway VLAN with no FHRP
detectors.checks: A VLAN with >= 2 gateways where no end runs a first-hop-redundancy protocol — the second gateway does not actually back up the first.
detectors.healthy_value: an FHRP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) present on the gateways
detectors.abstains_when: the VLAN's gateways were not collected, or FHRP behaviour not captured

detectors.title: Down tracked object on a gateway
detectors.checks: A gateway switch with a tracked object in the DOWN state — the object the FHRP priority/route depends on has failed.
detectors.healthy_value: all tracked objects up (or none tracked)
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or the tracking output not captured for the gateway

detectors.title: Fake first-hop redundancy on a VLAN
detectors.checks: A VLAN whose >= 2 gateways have inconsistent FHRP — missing on one end, mixed protocols, different groups/virtual-IPs, or two active routers (split-brain).
detectors.healthy_value: one FHRP group, one virtual IP, one active router per VLAN
detectors.abstains_when: the VLAN's gateway switches were not all collected (an unseen far-end gateway is not evidence of consistency)

detectors.title: Accidental STP root (default bridge priority)
detectors.checks: A VLAN whose spanning-tree root runs the default bridge priority, so the root was won on a MAC tiebreak, not engineered — it can move on a cutover.
detectors.abstains_when: the root switch for the VLAN was not collected, or spanning-tree output not captured (MST instances are out of scope)

detectors.title: STP root not co-located with the L3 gateway
detectors.checks: A VLAN whose spanning-tree root is a switch that does NOT host the VLAN's L3 gateway SVI, so intra-VLAN traffic to the gateway hairpins through the root.
detectors.abstains_when: the root switch or the VLAN's gateway switch was not collected

detectors.title: No centralized AAA (CIS 1.4)
detectors.checks: The running-config has no central AAA (TACACS+/RADIUS) — authentication is local / line-based only.
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device (parse_security returns {} -> the CIS finding cannot be emitted)

detectors.title: Reversible privileged-EXEC secret (CIS 1.2.1)
detectors.checks: The device uses a reversible 'enable password' (Type-0/7) instead of a strong 'enable secret'.
detectors.healthy_value: status == pass (strong enable secret) or na (none present)
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device

detectors.title: SNMPv1/v2c community exposure (CIS 3.1)
detectors.checks: A read or read-write SNMP v1/v2c community is present (cleartext, guessable) rather than SNMPv3 auth+priv.
detectors.healthy_value: status == pass (no v1/v2c community; SNMPv3 only)
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device

detectors.title: Telnet VTY transport enabled (CIS 2.1)
detectors.checks: A VTY line permits telnet (or the NX-OS telnet feature is on) — cleartext management access.
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device

detectors.title: No logging / audit trail (CIS 6.2)
detectors.checks: The running-config configures no syslog host / buffered logging — no audit trail across the migration.
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device (config absence never reads as configured logging — the bare NX-OS false-health class)

detectors.title: Undefined ACL / route-map / object-group reference
detectors.checks: A referenced ACL/route-map/object-group/prefix-list that is never defined — it silently does nothing, a migration-breaker.
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured for the device (an un-captured config is not a clean config)

detectors.title: Device past last-day-of-support (LDoS)
detectors.checks: A device whose model's LDoS date is in the past relative to the assessment date — no vendor support of any kind remains.
detectors.abstains_when: model not resolvable in the offline eoldb KB, or device model not collected (band == Unknown, never a silent Active)

detectors.title: Device past end-of-sale but not yet LDoS
detectors.checks: A device past its end-of-sale date but still within the support tail (a distinct, smaller population than Past-LDoS).
detectors.abstains_when: model not resolvable in the eoldb KB, or device model not collected (band == Unknown)

detectors.title: MAC-flap events in the log buffer
detectors.checks: MAC-flap / MAC-move events in the buffered log (a bridging loop or a dual-homed endpoint moving between ports).
detectors.abstains_when: the device's buffered log was not collected (per_device.collected == False); the buffer is a bounded window so counts are floors

detectors.title: Err-disable events in the log buffer
detectors.checks: Err-disable transitions in the buffered log (a port protection mechanism tripping).
detectors.abstains_when: the device's buffered log was not collected (per_device.collected == False)

detectors.title: Interface link-flap in the log buffer
detectors.checks: An interface with repeated down transitions in the buffered log (a flapping link).
detectors.healthy_value: no interface at/over the link-flap floor
detectors.abstains_when: the device's buffered log was not collected (per_device.collected == False)

detectors.title: QoS enabled with no trust boundary
detectors.checks: Global QoS is enabled but no port defines a trust boundary, so ingress CoS/DSCP is remarked to 0 fleet-wide — QoS actively harms traffic in this state.
detectors.healthy_value: a defined trust boundary (or QoS not globally enabled)
detectors.abstains_when: no full running-config captured (per_device.assessable == False -> device declared not-assessable, never scored healthy)

detectors.title: Voice VLAN without an edge QoS policy
detectors.checks: A voice-VLAN access port carrying no trust statement, auto-QoS macro or service-policy — phone markings are not honored at the edge.
detectors.abstains_when: no full running-config captured (per_device.assessable == False)

detectors.title: Open attack surface for a landmark advisory
detectors.checks: A configuration surface that is open (exposed web UI / SNMP v1-v2c / Smart Install / telnet / SSHv1 / IKEv1 / small services) and maps to a landmark public advisory — 'surface open', never a per-release vulnerability verdict.
detectors.healthy_value: surface closed on every screened kind
detectors.abstains_when: no running-config captured (per_device.config_assessable == False -> the surface layer is declared not-assessable, never 'closed')

detectors.title: Software train in a replace/verify lifecycle band
detectors.checks: A cautious software-TRAIN lifecycle band derived from the collected version/platform (replace / verify-with-Cisco / current-era), verify-with-Cisco wording.
detectors.abstains_when: software version not captured for the device (sw_version == '(not captured)' -> the train layer is not assessable)

detectors.title: Control-plane CPU hot
detectors.checks: A 5-minute CPU average at/above the hot threshold — no headroom for a reconvergence event or a config push (a single point-in-time sample).
detectors.healthy_value: band == OK (5-min CPU below the elevated threshold)
detectors.abstains_when: capacity commands not collected (per_device.collected == False -> band == Unknown, never a silent OK)

detectors.title: Processor memory low
detectors.checks: Free processor memory at/below the critical percentage — MALLOCFAIL risk under the table churn a migration adds.
detectors.healthy_value: band == OK (free memory above the low threshold)
detectors.abstains_when: capacity commands not collected (per_device.collected == False -> band == Unknown)

detectors.title: Port utilization headroom
detectors.checks: Per-device switched-port utilization (active vs total ports) — how much access capacity remains before the migration adds endpoints.
detectors.abstains_when: device physical inventory not collected (no capacity row emitted for the device)

detectors.title: PoE power-budget headroom
detectors.checks: Per-device PoE budget draw vs capacity — whether adding powered endpoints (phones/APs/cameras) would exceed the power budget.
detectors.abstains_when: PoE inventory not collected for the device (no PoE capacity row emitted)

detectors.title: Native VLAN 1 on inter-switch trunks
detectors.checks: An inter-switch trunk carrying the default VLAN 1 as the native (untagged) VLAN — a hygiene and VLAN-hopping exposure.
detectors.healthy_value: a dedicated, unused native VLAN on inter-switch trunks
detectors.abstains_when: device not collected, or trunk/switchport detail not captured for the port

detectors.title: Native-VLAN mismatch across a trunk
detectors.checks: The two ends of an inter-switch trunk disagree on the native (untagged) VLAN — a silent L2 leak between the two VLANs.
detectors.healthy_value: both ends agree on the native VLAN
detectors.abstains_when: either end of the trunk was not collected (an un-collected far end is not evidence of agreement)

detectors.title: Flat L3 (no VRF and no gateway ACLs)
detectors.checks: Gateways exist but every one sits in the global VRF with no applied ACL — a flat L3 with no isolation between application domains.
detectors.healthy_value: a non-global VRF or a gateway ACL present
detectors.threshold: n_gateways > 0 AND distinct non-global VRFs == 0 AND n_with_acl == 0
detectors.abstains_when: no gateway SVIs collected (no gateway evidence -> the flat-L3 verdict is not assessable)

summary.note: Each row DESCRIBES a live detector, grounded in its source; it does not re-run detection. 'abstains_when' is the coverage-honest guard — the condition under which the detector ABSTAINS (maps to ssot.abstention_reason's 'not_collected') instead of passing, so a blind spot never reads as healthy. It is never empty for an evidence-gated detector.

checks.title: Distribution/core tier present
checks.observed: 2 L3 node(s) (gateway SVI or routing adjacency) front 1 L2 access node(s).
checks.implication: A defined L3 tier bounds failure domains and gives the migration a stable anchor.
checks.recommendation: Carry the tiering into the target design; keep gateway functions at the distribution tier.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — hierarchical access/distribution/core model

checks.title: No daisy-chained access switches
checks.observed: Every observed access uplink lands on the L3 tier.
checks.implication: Failure domains stay bounded per closet.
checks.recommendation: Preserve the star topology in the target design.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — each access switch homes to the distribution layer

checks.title: Dual-homed access uplinks
checks.observed: 1 of 1 access switch(es) reach exactly ONE in-fleet neighbour: access1.
checks.implication: A single uplink (or single upstream switch) is a per-closet single point of failure — one optic, one linecard or one upstream chassis takes the closet down.
checks.recommendation: Dual-home each listed switch to two distribution nodes (or at minimum two linecards) as part of the migration build.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — redundant uplinks from every access switch

checks.title: First-hop redundancy on every gateway
checks.observed: VLAN(s) 30 are served by a SINGLE gateway with no FHRP peer.
checks.implication: Losing that one gateway device black-holes every endpoint on the VLAN — the highest-impact availability exposure a campus carries, and a migration-readiness FAIL.
checks.recommendation: Add an FHRP peer (or move the VLAN behind a redundant gateway pair) BEFORE any migration wave touches these VLANs.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — FHRP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) on every shared gateway

checks.title: Redundant power supplies
checks.observed: Power-supply inventory was not captured for any device.
checks.recommendation: Include 'show environment power' / inventory output in collection.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — N+1 power on aggregation nodes

checks.title: No keystone single point of failure
checks.observed: Losing core1 strands 3 endpoint(s).
checks.implication: Endpoint dependency is concentrated — these devices ARE the availability budget.
checks.recommendation: Verify each keystone's redundancy (uplinks, power, supervisor) and sequence them with the most conservative cutover plan (their waves carry the widest blast radius).
checks.reference: Availability analysis — single-device blast radius

checks.title: Deterministic STP root at the distribution tier
checks.observed: Access switch(es) hold the STP root: access1 roots 1 VLAN(s).
checks.implication: A root on an access closet means the L2 tree converges around the smallest box in the fabric — default (un-pinned) priorities usually caused it, and any new switch can silently steal the root.
checks.recommendation: Pin root primary/secondary priorities on the distribution pair for every VLAN.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — pin the STP root (priority) at the distribution layer

checks.title: Edge protection (BPDU Guard) on access ports
checks.observed: BPDU Guard state was not captured for the access ports.
checks.recommendation: Include 'show spanning-tree interface detail' (or run-config) in collection.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — PortFast + BPDU Guard on every edge port

checks.title: VLAN 1 not used for user traffic
checks.observed: Trunks with native VLAN 1 on 3 switch(es): access1, core1, core2.
checks.implication: Native VLAN 1 on inter-switch trunks exposes untagged control-plane crosstalk and is flagged by the hardening baseline.
checks.recommendation: Set the native VLAN to a dedicated unused VLAN on the listed trunks.
checks.reference: Cisco hardening guidance — keep user traffic and trunk native VLAN off VLAN 1

checks.title: Bounded broadcast domains
checks.observed: Largest observed VLAN carries 3 endpoint(s) — within the conventional envelope.
checks.implication: Broadcast domains are bounded.
checks.recommendation: Keep VLAN sizing within a /24-/23 of endpoints in the target design.
checks.reference: Campus design guidance — constrain broadcast domains (≈ a /23 of endpoints per VLAN)

checks.title: Trunks pruned to required VLANs
checks.observed: All 2 trunk(s) with captured lists are pruned.
checks.implication: VLAN scope stays bounded per closet.
checks.recommendation: Maintain pruning in the per-wave port maps.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — prune trunk allowed-VLAN lists to the required set

checks.title: Every access VLAN has a gateway in scope
checks.observed: All 2 access VLAN(s) terminate on an in-scope gateway SVI.
checks.implication: The L2/L3 boundary is fully accounted for.
checks.recommendation: Keep the gateway register in the LLD as the addressing source of truth.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — every user VLAN terminates on a known, redundant gateway

checks.title: DHCP relay on endpoint-serving gateways
checks.observed: 1 endpoint-carrying VLAN(s) have a gateway with no DHCP relay configured: VLAN(s) 30.
checks.implication: If those clients use central DHCP, the missing helper is a silent post-cutover black hole (the classic day-1 failure); if addressing is static/local this is by design.
checks.recommendation: Confirm the addressing model per VLAN; add helpers where central DHCP is intended before the carrying wave.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — ip helper-address on every client-serving SVI

checks.title: Single IGP, controlled redistribution
checks.observed: 3 redistribution edge(s) observed.
checks.implication: Every extra protocol and redistribution point is a loop/suboptimal-routing risk and a troubleshooting tax; migrations are when undocumented redistribution bites.
checks.recommendation: Plan convergence to a single IGP in the target design; until then, document each redistribution edge (route-map, direction, owner) in the LLD.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — one IGP where possible; document every redistribution boundary

checks.title: FHRP active aligned with the STP root
checks.observed: No VLAN has both a known FHRP active gateway and an observed root bridge.
checks.recommendation: Collect 'show standby'/'show spanning-tree' together to enable this check.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — co-locate the FHRP active gateway with the STP root per VLAN

checks.title: Access uplink oversubscription within 20:1
checks.observed: 1 access switch(es) measured; worst provisioned ratio 1:1.
checks.implication: Uplink capacity is within the conventional envelope.
checks.recommendation: Re-validate ratios whenever the target design changes uplink counts or speeds.
checks.reference: Cisco campus rule of thumb — ≤20:1 access→distribution, ≤4:1 distribution→core

checks.title: Port-capacity headroom for growth
checks.observed: access1 at 100.0% port utilisation.
checks.implication: A full closet forces ad-hoc daisy-chaining (see HIER-2) the day a port is needed.
checks.recommendation: Size replacement hardware with ≥10% spare ports per listed closet.
checks.reference: Capacity planning — keep ~10% port headroom per closet

checks.title: No operational drift / false health
checks.observed: 1 lower-severity drift finding(s).
checks.implication: Low-grade drift compounds; the migration touch is the cheapest moment to clear it.
checks.recommendation: Fold the items into the per-wave work orders.
checks.reference: Assessment doctrine — configured is not healthy; up is not healthy

checks.title: Clean configuration hygiene
checks.observed: 2 undefined reference(s) across 1 device(s): core1.
checks.implication: A referenced-but-undefined ACL/route-map fails OPEN or CLOSED depending on platform — either way it is latent surprise during cutover.
checks.recommendation: Resolve or remove each undefined reference before its device migrates.
checks.reference: Operational hygiene — no undefined references in running configuration

checks.title: Collection confidence
checks.observed: Collection is complete across the fleet.
checks.implication: The review stands on full evidence.
checks.reference: Assessment doctrine — state collection blind spots explicitly

checks.title: Cross-domain dependencies & interoperability declared
checks.observed: The fleet spans 2 switch NOS families (2× IOS, 1× NXOS).
checks.implication: A multi-NOS estate must keep feature / CLI / automation parity across families, and any cross-family migration (e.g. IOS->NX-OS) is an explicit interoperability step, not a like-for-like swap — undeclared, it surfaces as a cutover surprise.
checks.recommendation: Declare the platform-dependency + interoperability surface in the HLD (the design interoperability footprint) and validate cross-family behaviour during NRFU.
checks.reference: Cisco Advanced Services design-review practice — declare platform dependencies & interop

checks.title: Management-plane hardening (CIS baseline)
checks.observed: 1 device(s) grade WEAK (a high-severity hardening check fails): core1; 1 more grade partial.
checks.implication: A weak management plane (open HTTP/Smart Install, missing AAA, default communities) is the attack surface that turns a migration window into an incident.
checks.recommendation: Apply the generated remediation snippets to the WEAK devices first — before any maintenance window publicises change activity.
checks.reference: CIS Cisco IOS Benchmark — AAA, NTP, logging, SSHv2/VTY, SNMPv3 hardening

checks.title: Segmentation enforced at the L3 boundary
checks.observed: 1 VRF(s) in use; 2 of 5 gateway SVIs carry an ACL.
checks.implication: Partial enforcement leaves unpoliced inter-segment paths.
checks.recommendation: Close the unpoliced SVIs (or fold them into a VRF) in the target design.
checks.reference: Segmentation guidance — enforce inter-segment policy at the L3 boundary (VRF / gateway ACL)

checks.title: No hardware past end-of-support
checks.observed: 1 device(s) past end-of-sale, 1 approaching LDoS.
checks.implication: Support windows are closing; replacement lead times belong in the plan now.
checks.recommendation: Schedule the EoS platforms into the early waves of the replacement plan.
checks.reference: Cisco EoX policy — no TAC/software support past last-day-of-support

checks.title: One software image per platform
checks.observed: Every platform runs a single image.
checks.implication: Troubleshooting and rollback are uniform per model.
checks.recommendation: Pin the images as the minimum-version baseline in the LLD.
checks.reference: AS LLD convention — minimise image variance per platform
